react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on a coherent biological story centred on Phase I xenobiotic metabolism, polyamine homeostasis, and arachidonic acid signalling. Under RaMP multi-DB ORA, the top hit was REACT:R-HSA-211945 (Phase I - Functionalization of compounds, FDR = 0.0015) driven by coumarin and putrescine. The same ORA ranked REACT:R-HSA-211859 (Biological oxidations, FDR = 0.0021) with the same two metabolites, reflecting CYP-mediated monooxygenation chemistry that activates coumarin. A parallel m/z-directed mummichog analysis identified MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism as the top pathway (p = 0.014), with the input compound 20-Hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (20-HETE, KEGG:C14748) confirmed as a direct member alongside inferred HETE/EET congeners (5-HETE, 15-HETE, 8,9-EET, 11,12-EET, 14,15-EET). The mummichog result also surfaced MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism (p = 0.038) as a secondary hit, linking coumarin to detoxification circuitry. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA returned KEGG:hsa00480 (Glutathione metabolism, p = 0.052) anchored on putrescine, consistent with the polyamine-oxidation theme visible across RaMP (Agmatine biosynthesis, PAO oxidations, polyamine interconversion). The SMPDB Spironolactone Action Pathway (SMPDB:SMP00134) appeared as a single-compound hit for spironolactone, its aldosterone-receptor antagonism producing a distinct clinical-metabolomics signature. Cross-paradigm consensus is strongest for (1) xenobiotic/Phase I metabolism — coumarin is a consistent driver across ORA and mummichog, and (2) polyamine metabolism — putrescine anchors multiple Reactome branches with very high fold-enrichment. The 20-HETE signal is unique to the mummichog m/z layer, illustrating the value of network-aware methods for lipid mediators.

Under RaMP multi-DB ORA, the top hit was REACT:R-HSA-211945 (Phase I - Functionalization of compounds) with FDR = 0.0015, driven by coumarin and putrescine, followed by REACT:R-HSA-211859 (Biological oxidations) at FDR = 0.0021 with the same two metabolites. Spironolactone independently hit SMPDB:SMP00134 (Spironolactone Action Pathway, FDR = 0.0041) and the polyamine-interconversion cluster including REACT:R-HSA-351143 (Agmatine biosynthesis), REACT:R-HSA-141334 (PAOs oxidise polyamines to amines), and REACT:R-HSA-351200 (Interconversion of polyamines), all driven by putrescine.
